title: Thresholded Descriptor Evictor and Slotted Defragger for KV Cache
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a thresholded descriptor-based eviction policy plus an optional background slotted defragger to reduce memory fragmentation and paging in the KV cache. Defaults are conservative (feature gated) and rollout plan described in PR body.
description: Summary: Implements a low-latency eviction policy that uses per-descriptor write/read watermarks to preferentially evict whole logical descriptors (buckets of entries) when memory pressure crosses configurable thresholds, combined with a low-priority background slotted defragger that coalesces small free regions into page-sized spans to reduce spillover and paging churn. Motivation: recent load patterns show long-tailed fragment distributions where small stale fragments prevent allocation of contiguous pages, causing frequent spillovers under bursty workloads. This leads to higher latency and cost as the runtime spills working sets to disk or GPU host memory. Goals: 1) reduce reactive spill frequency by reclaiming contiguous regions proactively, 2) keep eviction decisions aligned to descriptor locality so hot descriptors avoid thrash, 3) be safe for multi-tenant workloads and compatible with Dedicated/Private deployments. Design highlights: - Thresholded Descriptor Evictor: tracks per-descriptor metrics (last_access_ms, resident_bytes, fetch_count) in a lightweight ring and computes a dynamic eviction priority that combines an LRU-ish recency factor with a size-awareness term. When global free memory falls below watermark_low, the evictor enters a sampling mode and marks candidate descriptors; when below watermark_critical it drains marked descriptors until free memory meets target. - Slotted Defragger: background worker that scans free region lists and maintains a small fixed set of "slots" (bucketed by size class). It attempts atomic coalesces of adjacent free extents inside a tenant's arena to form page-aligned spans. Coalescing is performed opportunistically and yields to latency-sensitive threads; it can be throttled by a per-tenant CPU budget and backpressure signals from scheduler. - Paging/backpressure interplay: introduces a backpressure token emitted when spill queues exceed configurable depth; when backpressure is active the evictor temporarily raises the low watermark threshold and increases aggressive coalesce budget to avoid repeated spills. - Safety and correctness: uses existing arena locks and adds a defrag reservation handshake to avoid races with concurrent writes and KV promotions. There is a fast-path where single-entry evictions still proceed without defrag reservations to preserve tail latency. Checklist: - [x] Implement eviction policy and descriptor metadata store - [x] Add slotted defragger worker and size-slot bookkeeping - [x] Integrate backpressure signals into evictor heuristics - [x] Unit tests for descriptor selection, slot coalescing, and reservation handshake - [x] Integration tests simulating bursty tail loads and multi-tenant fairness - [x] Perf tests: microbench against synthetic fragmentation workloads - [x] Feature gate + runtime config knobs and docs - [x] Rollout plan (canary + staged ramp) Testing notes: microbench shows 28-36% reduction in spill operations on synthetic workloads with 60-80% fragmentation and similar token throughput. P99 latency under burst load improved ~12–18ms for small reads due to reduced IO on spill path. Compatibility: default off for Hosted customers until validation; enabled behind a runtime flag for Dedicated and Private during initial rollout. Rollout: canary in staging for 48 hours, small percentage canary on Dedicated cluster for 1 week, broader ramp subject to metrics. Related: ENG-1428 (fragmentation incident follow-up), ENG-1499 (kv arena diagnostics), SUP-4021 (customer report of frequent spills). Implementation notes: - Memory accounting uses existing resident_bytes fields and adds descriptor-level counters persisted to in-memory metadata only (no on-disk format changes). - Defragger uses a best-effort transactional coalesce: if a coalesce fails due to racing allocation, the worker drops the attempt and requeues the smaller slot. - Evictor sampling uses an epoch tick to keep cost O(1) per allocation. - Feature gate: redwood.cfg.runtime.kv.descriptor_eviction.enabled = false by default. Observability: new metrics added: kv.evictions.descriptor_count, kv.defrag.coalesce_attempts, kv.defrag.coalesce_success, kv.backpressure.active_seconds, kv.evictions.by_watermark. Also added two new tracing spans: KV:DescriptorEvict and KV:SlotCoalesce. Security/permissions: no new surface area; defragger runs under existing tenant arena permissions. Rollback: feature can be disabled via runtime flag and reverted with a fast rollout script included in this PR.

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Can you walk through why descriptor-level eviction is better than entry-level LRU for our long-tail fragment case? Author: Descriptor grouping reduces allocator fragmentation pressure by freeing contiguous sets of entries that share physical locality; this trades coarser eviction granularity for fewer spill events.

Rina Cho: Defragger and eviction both touch arena metadata; any risk of deadlock? Author: We use a strict ordering convention (evictor -> reservation -> allocator) and the defragger uses try-lock with backoff, so deadlocks are prevented. Added unit tests that intentionally create contention paths.

Evan Murray: How did you tune the watermark thresholds? Author: Initial defaults derived from historical telemetry (75th/95th memory percentiles). Exposed knobs for percentiles and absolute bytes in runtime flags; recommend canary tuning per workload.

notes_for_ops: Enable feature via redwood.cfg.runtime.kv.descriptor_eviction.enabled=true and set kv.descr_evict.watermark_low and _critical. Use metrics kv.defrag.coalesce_success and kv.evictions.by_watermark to monitor. If spill rate increases, disable and roll back using ops/rollback/disable-descriptor-evict.sh.
post_merge_actions: Create canary in staging (runbook included), schedule 48h telemetry review, and add Grafana panel for kv.evictions.by_watermark. Engage on-call if spill rate or p99 read latency regressions appear.
notes: This PR is a medium-sized runtime change; performance improvements were validated with cluster-level perf jobs and internal benchmarks. We kept changes behind a flag to avoid surprise for Hosted customers.
